97:2080.name: Our research combined interviews, surveys, and competitor analysis to understand the everyday realities of textured hair care and why so many people still struggle to find guidance they trust. Users repeatedly described relying on TikTok, YouTube, and Pinterest, but also expressed how these platforms often present surface-level tutorials, inconsistent advice, algorithm-driven misinformation, and content that rarely accounts for different curl types, porosities, or cultural context. Many felt overwhelmed by conflicting recommendations, frustrated by creators who skip essential steps, and unsupported when trying to translate viral trends into routines that actually work for their hair. These pain points revealed a major gap: people are searching for clear, reliable, culturally rooted education that goes deeper than entertainment. This shaped our approach to Braid, positioning it as a structured, trustworthy learning platform built on lived experience, expert insight, and the real needs shared across our community. Read Less

95:779.name: Property 1=Braid came into fruition when a group of designers and storytellers recognized how overwhelming and underrepresented textured hair education truly was. After I pitched the idea during a class project where we could form teams around concepts we believed in, that spark brought our group together for a dedicated 15-week build. What began in the classroom quickly deepened into an independent directed study, where we created our own curriculum, delivered self-defined projects, and pushed the work further with the guidance of a faculty mentor. Rooted in lived experience, community insight, and a shared commitment to bridge the gap between stylists and everyday people, we began shaping Braid into a trusted, modern resource that celebrates the beauty and complexity of textured hair.
